# Steam Turbines
# Operation
The boiler burns fuel from a removable Standard hopper or tank. It needs room oxygen and a water-filled internal reservoir. Fuel heat raises steam temperature and pressure; pressure limits electrical output while the turbine warms up or loses water. The turbine has a slow electrical ramp, so pair it with stored power for sudden loads.
Stop the machine and open its maintenance panel to install or remove a fuel module. Close the panel to add fuel or pour pure water into the reservoir. Examine the water, pressure and temperature gauges. The internal condenser returns most water; a little escapes as hot water vapor. Burning fuel also releases carbon dioxide into the room.
The basic 250u reservoir lasts about four hours at rated output. The water gauge reaches its low range near 10 percent; falling pressure throttles power and eventually trips the turbine. Refill and restart it manually. A basic 1500u tank of Welding Fuel lasts about two and a half hours at rated output. Wood, coal, plasma and fuel-grade plasma use the same Standard hopper as the Stirling generator. Weaker fuels require more stoking to hold boiler temperature.
# Damage
At 20 percent chassis damage, the boiler begins venting hot water vapor on damage steps. Further hits vent more water and lower pressure. A pressurized machine can burst if destroyed while running; its pressure blast cannot break floor tiles. Repairing the chassis restores its pressure sealing, but does not replace lost water.
